sources: Own knowledge of NPS climbing information and standard guide descriptions; names and elevations cross-checked against the local OpenStreetMap extract (washington-latest.osm.pbf). Elevations in feet; OSM elevations converted from meters.

features.name: Skyline Trailhead
features.note: highway=trailhead next to the Jackson Visitor Center / Paradise Climbing Information Center.

features.name: Skyline Trail (Paradise to Glacier Vista)
features.note: Paved then dirt trail; summer route climbs the Skyline Trail clockwise toward Glacier Vista.

features.name: Glacier Vista
features.note: tourism=viewpoint over the Nisqually Glacier; short Glacier Vista Trail spur.

features.name: Panorama Point
features.note: OSM has a peak node (2106 m) and a viewpoint node tagged 6800 ft. Climbers often take the Upper Skyline Trail above it.

features.name: Pebble Creek
features.note: Crossing where the maintained trail ends and the Muir Snowfield begins.

features.name: McClure Rock
features.note: Rock outcrop beside the lower route just above Pebble Creek (OSM 2243 m). Optional landmark.

features.name: Muir Snowfield
features.osm_name_if_any: Muir Snowfield (natural=glacier polygon); route line 'Camp Muir Route'
features.note: Permanent snowfield, no trail; whiteout navigation hazard. Route stays left (west) of Anvil Rock.

features.name: Moon Rocks
features.note: OSM natural=rock near the snowfield route; elevation estimated. Optional landmark.

features.name: Anvil Rock
features.note: Off-route landmark east of the snowfield (OSM 2921 m); former fire lookout site. Do not route through it.

features.name: Camp Muir
features.note: tourism=camp_site with public shelter, ranger hut and guide huts. Day-hike end point; climbers continue with a permit.

features.name: Cowlitz Glacier crossing
features.note: Short traverse east from Camp Muir across the Cowlitz Glacier to the Cathedral Rocks ridge. Cowlitz Glacier polygon not found in the local extract.

features.name: Cathedral Gap
features.note: Notch through the Cathedral Rocks ridge (OSM has 'Cathedral Rocks' as natural=ridge but no Cathedral Gap node). Loose rock and scree switchbacks.

features.name: Ingraham Glacier
features.note: Lower Ingraham Glacier from Cathedral Gap to Ingraham Flats and the toe of the Cleaver. Glacier polygon not in the local extract (likely an incomplete relation at the bbox edge).

features.name: Ingraham Flats
features.note: OSM tourism=camp_site at 3414 m (~11,200 ft). Common high camp.

features.name: The Bowling Alley
features.note: Traverse from Ingraham Flats across the Ingraham Glacier to the base of the Disappointment Cleaver, under rockfall and icefall from the Cleaver and Ingraham icefall. Move fast, no stopping. Exact limits vary by season.

features.name: Disappointment Cleaver
features.osm_name_if_any: Disappointment Cleaver (natural=ridge); route line 'Disappointment Cleaver Route'
features.note: Rock and snow ridge between the Ingraham and Emmons glaciers; route gains the ridge at its lower nose and climbs the spine.

features.name: High Break
features.note: Rest stop at the top of the Cleaver where the route steps onto the upper glacier. Name used by guide services; not in OSM.

features.name: Upper Ingraham / Emmons Glacier
features.note: Upper route switchbacks across the upper Ingraham and Emmons glaciers to the crater rim; line moves through the season with crevasses (ladders/wands placed by guides and rangers).

features.name: Crater rim
features.note: Southeast edge of the summit crater where the route tops out. Register Rock (OSM natural=rock) sits in the crater nearby.

features.name: Summit crater crossing
features.note: Walk across the east crater to the far (west/northwest) rim.

features.name: Columbia Crest
features.note: Highest point of Mount Rainier and Washington (OSM ele 4392 m). GNIS names the summit 'Crater Peak'; NPS and most sources use Columbia Crest.

unverified.name: The Icebox
unverified.found: No published guide or ranger text that I can cite names 'the Icebox' as a spot on the Disappointment Cleaver route. The local OSM extract has no 'Icebox' feature on Mount Rainier (the only match, 'Icebox Peak', is a 2473 m peak elsewhere in Washington). I did not search the web (outside this task's allowed sources). Left out of the feature list until someone can cite a ranger blog, NPS route brief, or guide-service page that uses the name for this route.
